# ASCII CRT — Style Prompt

> One monochrome terminal, and nothing on it but real characters on a monospace grid, glowing amber on dark curved glass. A sentence is typed with a blinking block cursor; its letters shake loose, fall and land cell by cell as a picture drawn only with those same letters (a moon plain, stars, the Earth rising); one soft second colour switches on once, with a flash; then the camera, which is only the size of the font, pushes into a single letter until it turns out to be made of lines of smaller text. Machine-calm, patient, one warm surprise.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

The film is **one terminal screen under one camera**, and the camera is the font size: bigger cells push in, smaller cells pull out. Every image (title, landscape, planet, subtitle) is real glyphs placed on a character grid and chosen by ink density, so negative space does the drawing. The signature is **the picture is made of the words**: the density ramp for every picture is built from the letters of the sentence that was just typed, so the landscape and the planet contain only those letters. Typed text, a blinking cursor and a log strip carry the story; it never leaves the glass.

Not an image behind an "ASCII filter" (every character is a glyph in a cell), not hacker green rain, not pixel art (no sprites, no free pixels), not a sci-fi HUD (no vector lines, no floating panels), not a slideshow (screens never crossfade; they decay, crumble, redraw or push), not live 3D (rebuilt in 2D: text layers, gradients, transforms).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Glyphs**: VT323 everywhere, cell 0.4 em × 0.8 em. Pictures on a fine grid of 8 × 16 px cells (20 px type, 240 columns); the typed sentence on 80 px cells (200 px type, 16 characters from x 320, cell top 380, baseline 508); the previous screen and the log rule on an 80-column terminal (21 px cells, 52.5 px type); the log line on 18 px cells (45 px type).
- **Density ramp from the sentence**: each distinct letter's ink coverage, measured from VT323 (drawn at 160 px with a 2.2 px stroke for beam spread), divided by the densest, times three brightness attributes (dim .42, normal .7, bold 1); levels closer than .018 are dropped, keeping the bolder. A cell's value m becomes L = (1.08 m)^1.05, gets a 4 × 4 ordered dither plus a small hash, and takes the nearest level; under 0.05 it stays blank. A sentence without small marks has a big gap below its sparsest glyph, so dark ground turns into true negative space.
- **The picture (a negative drawn in light, then sampled per cell)**: a horizon y = 600 + 240u² − 70u minus two noise ridges (u = x/W − 0.5); ground darker and sparser far away, brighter and denser near, with large dark "seas", a bright lip along the horizon (+0.3·e^(−dy/10)), 34 craters plus three large ones (at 0.2, 0.78, 0.47 of the width; radius 250, 190, 95; squash 0.22-0.46 with depth) whose bowls are black from the left rim and lit on the right inner wall, rims bright top-left; a sparse star field (one per cell, 0.45% of sky cells). The Earth: centre x 1180, radius 262, tilted 14° toward the viewer and rolled −0.22 rad, sun off-frame top left, albedo 0.14 + 0.82·land, clouds (latitude bands plus swirls) pulling albedo 85% toward 0.5, terminator smoothstep(−0.03, 0.1), limb brightening (1 − n_z)³·0.35, a faint atmosphere ring to 1.1 r; the night side is only scattered dots. The moon averages six samples per cell, the Earth four.
- **Glass**: warm near-black (#080502 measured; the source's unlit phosphor ≈ #090604), centre lifted toward the second surface; 3 px scanlines; corners sinking hard (the source's vignette 1 − 0.55·(0.35 r² + 0.9 x²y²)); a rounded screen (corner radius 0.09 of the half-size, barrel curvature 0.045) set in a near-black bezel; a faint 3% reflection top left; flicker ±0.6%. **No RGB grille**: a monochrome tube has none.
- **Glow**: the typed sentence carries a three-step bloom (6, 22, 60 px); the planet sits in a soft halo of its colour; anything redrawn per step carries no shadow of its own.
- **Afterglow**: anything that goes out decays like P3 phosphor, τ = 0.12 s (×1.25 at the 15 s pace).
- **LOG strip**: a rule of 80 dim `-` glyphs at y 900, an inverse-video ` LOG ` tag, `>` and the line at column 8; it lives outside the zooming grid, which is clipped at y 898.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the glass; `--latar-2` only lifts its centre (9%).
- `--utama-di-latar` is the phosphor ramp of every picture: dim and normal levels mix it 47% and 76% into the glass (the source's dim orange of a P3 tube), full drive is `--panas`, a landing flash goes one step above.
- `--panas` is the overexposed core, `--utama-di-latar` mixed 45/55 into `--teks`: lemon on the default amber (the film's core clips to #fffc31), and darker, never lighter, on a pale brand because `--teks` is dark there. The typed sentence and the cursor use it.
- `--utama` is light, not ink: every glow and halo, the inverse ` LOG ` tag and the name bar of the ending; on a pale brand the glow nearly disappears into white instead of smudging dark.
- `--aksen` / `--aksen-di-latar` is the **one soft second colour** (the source's Earth blue #b8e0ff), used for one thing only, the emotional object (here the planet that answers), switched on once with a hard cut and a flash, never taken back. Its ramp mixes 45% and 74% into the glass, full drive 55% toward white.
- `--teks` sets the log line and typed details; `--teks-redup` labels; `--teks-di-utama` text on inverse bars. Brightness and inverse video are the only other tools.
- Fixed: black for the bezel and the corners; white only inside the overexposure mixes.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries what is typed big: the sentence at 200 px (max width 1440 px, so a wider brand font wraps to two lines above the log), the counted figure at 168 px, the ending's name at 132 px in inverse video, the previous screen at 52.5 px.
- `--font-isi` carries the log at 45 px, labels at 44 px and the ending's details at 72 px.
- `--font-kode` (VT323, never replaced by a brand) draws every picture at 20 / 16 px, the falling letters at 36 px and the inner text of a pushed-in letter at 18.75 / 15 px. The ramp's coverage numbers are measured for this font, so a picture font change means measuring again.
- When the brand has none: VT323 for both; IBM Plex Mono 400/600 for a cleaner, newer terminal.

## 5. Motion quality

The source film runs at 100 BPM (a beat 0.6 s); the 15 s example plays its 12 s section at 1.25×, so multiply the source numbers below by 1.25 for that pace.

- **Characters jump, they do not slide.** Typing, counters and pictures change cell by cell; only three things move continuously: the grid scale (camera), the glass, and letters in a transformation.
- **The previous screen** scales 1 → 3.8 around its prompt (eio, 0.6 s) while it decays (τ 0.12): the push that opens the section.
- **Typing**: 0.12 s per character, even; the block cursor (0.88 × 1.56 of a cell, inset 0.06 / 0.22) is solid while typing, then flashes on the beats: lit 0.3 s, then decaying. The idle log prompt blinks with a 1 s period.
- **The collapse** (t = 0 at the first beat after the hold): letters shake ±3 px at 24 fps for 0.7 s while a ghost copy slides 26 px down at 45%; each letter dims from 100% to 25% as its particles leave (about 1.6 s), then decays.
- **Particles** start at random points inside their source letter at 45 px, shrink to the 20 px grid within the first 45% of the flight, fall with x on a smoothstep and y as u·(0.6 + 0.4u); ground cells depart so they arrive 0.6 + 1.35·(1 − depth) + 0.28 r s after the collapse (bottom rows first), stars 1 + 2.2 r s, Earth cells fall behind the horizon and rise from it 1.75 + 1.5·height + 0.2 r s (bottom first, 0.5 s ease-out). Every landing flashes 1 + 0.9·e^(−t/0.12).
- **The colour switch** happens in one frame on its beat, with a flash 1 + 0.6·e^(−t/0.25); then the planet rises 64 px (four cell rows) with eio over 3 s, grid-locked.
- **Counter** (example): digits roll in integer steps for 0.8 s, power3.out.
- **Push into a letter**: the cell grows 8 → 300 px over 1.4 s, eio on a logarithmic scale; the target glides to its spot with smoothstep(min(1, 2.5k)); between cells of 70 and 190 px the letters cross-fade into lines of log text, 40 sub-cells per cell; inside the target's strokes full (1.15), neighbours 0.2, outside 0.06 and 0.03. The source pushes again 300 → 450 px after a 1 s hold.

## 6. Camera grammar

The only camera is the grid scale, plus glass power states. The zoomed grid stops at the log strip.

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Static terminal, cursor blinking | waiting, procedure, machine time | a question, a countdown, a queue, a log being read |
| Previous screen pushed past (1 → 3.8×, decaying) | a cut by moving through, not across | the opening, a new chapter |
| Push in (cells grow, log scale, eio) | attention, intimacy | one line, a name, a decision being typed |
| Pull out (cells shrink) | context, scale | a title becoming line 1 of a list, one entry among thousands |
| Push into a single glyph (cell 8 → 300 px) | hidden depth: what a symbol is made of | a letter made of messages, a pixel made of people, a logo made of names |
| Text becomes image (letters fall, land cell by cell) | words turning into a world | a sentence becoming a landscape, data becoming a map |
| Grid-locked rise (whole rows) | something arriving within the picture | a planet, a sun, a product rising over a horizon |
| Power on / off, degauss | birth, death, shock | a machine waking, an ending, a jolt |

## 7. Native moves

- **Typed on the beat.** One sentence in big phosphor glyphs at 0.12 s per character, then held while the cursor flashes on the beats. *Fits content like:* "ADA YANG DENGAR?" from a lonely radio operator; a shop's "MASIH BUKA?" at midnight; a creator's first line of a new series; a teacher's question to the class; the first clue of a mystery.
- **The picture is made of the words.** The sentence shakes, sheds a ghost, and its letters fall and land cell by cell as a picture whose density ramp holds only those letters. *Fits content like:* a question falling into a moon plain; a recipe crumbling into the dish; a poem becoming the town it describes; a class motto becoming the campus.
- **One colour, once.** The whole screen is one phosphor; on one beat, the object that matters switches to a soft second colour with a flash and keeps it, then rises a few rows. *Fits content like:* the Earth answering in ice blue; a first green leaf in a farm's data log; a child's drawing in a server room; the one sold-out item in a shop's stock list.
- **Font size is the camera.** A logarithmic push until one letter fills a third of the screen and is itself lines of smaller text, the neighbours dimmed so the shape reads before the text. *Fits content like:* a letter made of the log of replies; a brand's initial made of customer names; a year made of its headlines; a heart made of messages to a creator.
- **The log file.** A dashed rule, an inverse ` LOG ` tag and a prompt tell the story in short typed lines while the picture works above it. *Fits content like:* a launch day; a rescue; a class schedule; a long night told by a machine.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Performance (live preview).** Rebuild glyph strings only from the list of live cells, a few times a second, and split a big picture into bands of rows so unchanged bands are not laid out again. Never put a text shadow on glyph layers that are redrawn. Compute a moving picture once and move it by whole rows under a fixed clip instead of re-sampling it per step. During a push, let the world re-rasterise once per octave of scale (compositor-scaled in between) and sharp again when it stops; per-frame re-raster of big text drops the preview to half speed. Composite the per-frame flicker layer, merge static glass layers into one, draw particles as a few sheets of real text that only move.
- **Every dark pixel becoming a character** fills the ground with noise: threshold, use the ramp's gap, leave shadows blank.
- **Noise-textured subjects** read as blobs: silhouettes, a dark sparse background, a dot-only night side, one light direction.
- **Grid alignment**: picture layers share one cell size and origin, or pictures drift across columns. A cell's centre is (j + 0.5)·16, not (j + 1)·8.
- **Readability**: the log strip stays clear; typed lines over a picture get the glass colour behind their cells, as if overwritten.
- **Light brands**: glows come from `--utama` (they fade into white), pictures from `--utama-di-latar` (they read), the hot core leans toward `--teks` (it darkens).
- **Transitions** happen on the screen, never as a crossfade between two screens; the second colour appears once.

## Measured from the references

- The reference is one continuous 12 s shot (source film 29.95-41.95 s), no cuts, one internal change at 11.1 s (the push into a letter); dark (mean luma 16.5 of 255), motion energy 2.55.
- Palette by share: #080502 glass 83%, #342513 lifted glass 12%, #a2821a phosphor 3%, #7a8691 the second colour 2%; the source's phosphor parameters: amber (1, 0.69, 0), darks (1, 0.40, 0.02), overexposure (1, 0.92, 0.72), Earth (0.72, 0.88, 1).
- Beats (source seconds): typing 30.2-32.0, cursor beats 32.07, 32.4, 33.0, collapse 33.6, colour switch 37.2, rise to 40.2, push 40.2-41.6.

## Variation space

Who types, what the screen is for, the grids, the path of the camera and whether the second colour appears at all are free. Structures: a chat log across one night with timestamps as scene headers; a system manual whose diagrams are ASCII and one page goes wrong; a machine's day as scheduled jobs that each draw what they do. Openings: mid-scroll stopping on one line; a dot-matrix printout feeding up; a crash dump first. Endings: the buffer scrolls away until only the prompt remains; a screen saver drifts over the idle screen; the cursor stops blinking and stays lit; a pull back off the glass to the room the terminal stands in.

# ASCII CRT: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.5, medium 2.4, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: the old screen pushes past and decays; one question typed evenly in big phosphor glyphs, the block cursor flashing on the beats
- id: layar lama terdorong lewat dan padam; satu pertanyaan diketik rata dengan huruf fosfor besar, kursor blok berkedip mengikuti ketukan

## problem

- en: an error line types out in inverse video, the cursor stalls and blinks over it
- id: baris galat diketik dalam video terbalik, kursor macet dan berkedip di atasnya

## fact

- en: the sentence shakes, its letters fall and land cell by cell as a picture drawn only with those same letters
- id: kalimat bergetar, hurufnya jatuh dan mendarat sel demi sel menjadi gambar yang hanya tersusun dari huruf-huruf itu

## step

- en: one log line per step on the LOG strip with a timestamp, the picture above redrawn cell by cell
- id: satu baris log per langkah di strip LOG dengan jam, gambar di atasnya digambar ulang per sel

## compare

- en: two glyph pictures side by side on one grid; the better one switches to the second colour with a flash
- id: dua gambar huruf berdampingan di satu grid; yang lebih baik berganti ke warna kedua sambil berkilat

## number

- en: the picture switches to the one soft second colour with a flash and rises a few rows; the figure rolls, fast then slow
- id: gambar berganti ke satu warna kedua sambil berkilat lalu naik beberapa baris; angka berguling, cepat lalu melambat

## proof

- en: a log-scale push by glyph size until one letter fills the screen, made of lines of smaller text: the records
- id: zoom lewat ukuran huruf sampai satu huruf memenuhi layar, ternyata tersusun dari baris teks kecil: catatannya

## offer

- en: the offer typed by the machine as an inverse-video header, price beside it, cursor blinking
- id: penawaran diketik mesin sebagai judul video terbalik, harga di sampingnya, kursor berkedip

## cta

- en: name as an inverse-video bar, time and contact typed fast below, cursor blinking, held 2 s
- id: nama sebagai pita video terbalik, jadwal dan kontak diketik cepat di bawahnya, kursor berkedip, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the last line typed slowly, the cursor stops blinking and stays lit, held 2 s
- id: baris terakhir diketik pelan, kursor berhenti berkedip dan tetap menyala, diam 2 detik
